title: NNSA modernization can carry a large contract base without clear criteria for separable deliverables and lessons
source_unit: GAO-26-108409, National Nuclear Security Administration: Use of Line Items in Management and Operating Contracts Could Be Improved
geography: United States nuclear security enterprise; NNSA headquarters, field offices, and government-owned contractor-operated sites

observations.period: FY2025 and 2026 GAO review; NNSA modernization planning over the next decade

denominator.unit: NNSA management-and-operating contracts covering the nuclear security enterprise

annual_contract_scale.value: NNSA spends over $20 billion per year on nine management-and-operating contracts; it spent close to $24 billion in FY2025

modernization_scale.value: NNSA plans to spend almost $200 billion over the next decade modernizing nuclear-weapons production and research infrastructure

accountability_gap.value: NNSA had not documented criteria for when contracting officers should separate tasks into line or subline items, reducing assurance that choices were consistent and appropriate

learning_gap.value: NNSA had not fully assessed and documented lessons learned from using line items to guide future acquisition policy and avoid ineffective administrative approaches

downstream_outcome.value: the report does not establish whether separate line items changed contractor performance, cost, schedule, construction delivery, readiness, safety, or external deterrence

observations.method: GAO reviewed NNSA management-and-operating contracts, compared line-item use with Department of Energy acquisition policy and internal-control standards, and interviewed NNSA headquarters and field officials and contractor representatives.
observations.uncertainty: Contract-scale and planned-modernization figures do not establish completed capability. A missing criterion or documented lesson is a governance gap, not proof of waste, fraud, poor contractor performance, or failed nuclear-security outcomes. The review does not provide a project-level before-and-after estimate for line-item use.
observations.subgroup: NNSA headquarters, field offices, government-owned contractor-operated sites, management-and-operating contractors, construction projects, and future modernization portfolios.
observations.counterinterpretation: A single management-and-operating contract can preserve integration and reduce coordination cost; separate line items can also increase accountability or create administrative burden. The appropriate structure depends on deliverable separability, mission risk, and oversight capacity.

related_sources.claim: Official GAO report supplies contract scale, modernization scale, line-item governance gaps, method, and recommendations.

boundary: This record adds a contract-accountability and institutional-learning layer to domestic nuclear-security capacity: a large integrated contract base and modernization plan can coexist with unclear criteria for separable deliverables and incomplete lessons. It does not establish waste, fraud, failed capability, or changed geopolitical leverage.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official GAO landing page reviewed and retained as a source-page hash; the report PDF, contracts, and project-level performance data were not retained.
